description: Bluetooth room presence and a live house map for Home Assistant. See which room every iPhone, Android phone, Apple Watch and tag is in, on a floor plan with your lights, in 2D or 3D. Runs on a wall tablet in kiosk mode. Uses the ESPHome or Shelly Bluetooth proxies you already have, next to Bermuda or ESPresense. Demo: padspan.traks.ca/demo

latest_release.body:
## PadSpan HA v0.38.274 (STABLE)

Everything since the last stable release, v0.38.231, newest first.

### 0.38.274 — The stable after 0.38.231: lights you tap in the 3D house, power teams, a phone's room scan as a floor plan, steadier rooms, and safer saves (2026-11-21)

#### New
- **This is everything since 0.38.231 in one go,** written as how it works now. The betas' notes under it are the steps along the way; where they differ, this one is right.
- **Lights in the 3D house.** Tap a light in Live Aboard to switch it. Lights show as buttons under where they hang, can be moved in the 3D editor, string lights are drawn, and a room can work as one light switch. Unlocking a lock from the map asks first, white-only bulbs get a warmth slider, and a light's card has a Details link to Home Assistant's own window for it.
- **Power teams.** Smart bulbs on a wall dimmer, or lights that always have power, act as one light that follows the day. Lights found on after a restart are put right.
- **No floor plan? Ways to get one.** Start a blank floor, use a drawing you have, or upload a phone's room scan: its rooms, doors, windows and furniture come with it, and it finds its own place. When a plan is moved, what was placed on it can move with it, and lining up plans can suggest a fit.
- **Let Claude draw your rooms (experimental).** With an AI Task set up, Claude reads a plan and proposes room outlines that you check and keep.
- **Live Aboard** opens on the whole house with labels that follow the zoom, glass walls, a look for each screen, room chips and a room panel, kitchen and bathroom furniture, one-tap room sets, people and cars, covered patios, open decks and an Outside floor, and a ready-made Christmas tree.
- **Keys can keep their room (an option, off unless you turn it on).** Settings → Tracking → Home/Away Timeout: things no person carries can stay in their last room for hours. Every device's area sensor and tracker also gain `last_room`, the room it was last seen in.

#### Changed
- **Home Assistant 2024.8 or newer.** It said 2024.1, but before 2024.8 the sensors of the devices PadSpan tracks could not be added. Every release from 2024.8 to 2026.11 is now tested on each change.
- **Rooms are steadier.** A device that goes quiet keeps its room instead of drifting to another, possibly on another floor; a device nobody heard no longer "arrives"; a pinned beacon reports its room once; and a room change is never sent twice running. On a real house's four-hour recording, wrong room changes for devices that never moved halved compared with 0.38.231, and repeated room-change events went from 882 to 3.
- **Room tracking never waits.** It stalled for half a minute or more each time a calibration point was added, while a model only the "Learned model" setting uses was retrained; that model now trains in the background, and only when that setting is on. The health pages and the device list next to a busy street are much faster.
- **Lighter Home Assistant database.** Signal readings and other per-poll values are no longer written to Home Assistant's history; rooms, home or away and names still are.
- **A new install starts with Enhanced security on.** A home already set up keeps the switch as it has it.
- **Receivers' agreement in System Critics now means what it says**, and it no longer changes room decisions.

#### Fixed
- **Saves are checked.** A save of PadSpan's main files that does not reach the disk is reported in Settings → Repairs instead of passing silently, and the next good save takes the notice down.
- **A saved file PadSpan cannot read is kept,** renamed beside the others and named once in the log, instead of being written over.
- **Junk is refused in words:** a command with something missing, "nan" or "inf", numbers or texts too large to keep, and lists of the wrong kind. A settings save that is refused changes nothing at all.
- **Hidden devices stay hidden, and named devices stay listed** however long

detail.readme:
# PadSpan™ HA

### See which room every phone, watch and tag is in, live, on a plan of your home

[![PadSpan on a sample house: the whole house in 3D, lit rooms after dark with a guest's tag, tapping lights on the Atlas, then a new install's free Who's where now screen](./images/padspan-tour.webp)](https://padspan.traks.ca/demo/)

PadSpan is a Home Assistant integration for Bluetooth room presence. It listens to the Bluetooth proxies you already have, works out which room each phone, watch, tag and beacon is in, every 5 seconds, and shows it on a plan of your home: one floor at a time or all floors stacked. Your automations get room, distance and home/away sensors. The tracking runs locally.

▶️ **Try it in your browser: [padspan.traks.ca/demo](https://padspan.traks.ca/demo/)**, the real panel on a sample house. Nothing to install.

[![Open PadSpan in your Home Assistant](https://my.home-assistant.io/badges/hacs_repository.svg)](https://my.home-assistant.io/redirect/hacs_repository/?owner=gbroeckling&repository=padspanHA&category=integration) **Install:** one click opens PadSpan in **Settings → Marketplace** (Home Assistant 2026.11 and newer) or in HACS (older versions). Or search either one for PadSpan.

**What do you want PadSpan for?**

- **The whole house on one screen.** Every light, door, lock, alarm and sensor on a plan of your home, each in its room. Tap a light, see what's open, and a leak or smoke alarm turns its room red on every screen until someone resets it. Put it on a wall tablet with the free kiosk link. Needs only Home Assistant 2024.8 or newer. [See it](https://padspan.traks.ca/demo/?page=atlas)
- **Who's in which room.** Every phone, watch and tag, room by room, on every floor, with a week of replay. Needs at least one Bluetooth scanner: an ESPHome Bluetooth proxy, a Shelly Gen2 or newer set as a Bluetooth scanner ([one setting](https://padspan.traks.ca/guides/shelly-bluetooth-proxy/)), your Home Assistant machine's own Bluetooth, or an ESPresense node. One tells you home or away; one in each room you want told apart gives you rooms. [How many proxies do I need?](https://padspan.traks.ca/guides/bluetooth-proxies/) Already running Bermuda? Keep it: [PadSpan runs next to it](https://padspan.traks.ca/guides/bermuda/). [See it](https://padspan.traks.ca/demo/?page=panel)
- **Your floor plan.** Scan your rooms with an iPhone, start from your robot vacuum's map (experimental), or draw them, with split levels, room heights and lofts as they really are. Pro adds the house in 3D. [See it](https://padspan.traks.ca/demo/?page=atlas3d)
- **Every light in its place.** Free: every light on the map in its room, and a wall dimmer with its smart bulbs working as one light. Pro: each light exactly where it hangs, in its real shape. [See it](https://padspan.traks.ca/demo/?page=atlas)

**Free and open source (GPL-3.0).** PadSpan Pro adds exact placement on the Atlas, the touchscreen map of the whole house, plus Live Aboard (your house in 3D, like looking into a house in The Sims) and Furnish. **Try all of Pro free for 90 days, no card.** The anonymous usage report stays on during the trial ([how it works](./docs/PADSPAN_PRO.md#try-it-free-for-90-days)).

🎁 **PadSpan Pro free:** testers get two years of Pro while the anonymous usage report stays on ([how](./docs/PADSPAN_PRO.md#get-pro-free-by-testing-it)), and until December 31 the first 20 people to ask get a year ([details](https://github.com/gbroeckling/padspanHA/discussions/92)).

🌐 **Website: [padspan.traks.ca](https://padspan.traks.ca)** · 📖 **Guides:** [From the Marketplace to your first room](https://padspan.traks.ca/guides/get-started/) · [What can Home Assistant do once it knows the room?](https://padspan.traks.ca/guides/room-presence-automations/) · [Bermuda, NeonPlan 3D or PadSpan?](https://padspan.traks.ca/guides/bermuda-vs-neonplan/) · [Which room is my phone in?](https://padspan.traks.ca/guides/phone-room-presence/) · [Which Bluetooth tag works?](https://padspan.traks.ca/guides/bluetooth-tags/) · [Why does my phone jump between rooms?](https://padspan.traks.ca/guides/room-flapping/) · [How many Bluetooth proxies do I need?](https://padspan.traks.ca/guides/bluetooth-proxies/) · [Your Shellys can be Bluetooth proxies](https://padspan.traks.ca/guides/shelly-bluetooth-proxy/) · [Which floor plan for Home Assistant?](https://padspan.traks.ca/guides/floor-plans/) · [Your robot vacuum's map as your floor plan](https://padspan.traks.ca/guides/robot-vacuum-floor-plan/) · [Every floor of a big house on one wall](https://padspan.traks.ca/guides/large-homes/) · [Which touch screen for a PadSpan wall?](https://padspan.traks.ca/guides/wall-screens/) · [Bermuda and PadSpan together](https://padspan.traks.ca/guides/bermuda/) · [all guides](https://padspan.traks.ca/guides/) · 🎬 **Making a video or article?** [The creators kit](https://padspan.traks.ca/creators/)

<sub>The tour is the real panel on the demo's sample house, at real speed, with captions added. The full walkthrough video is on [padspan.traks.ca](https://padspan.traks.ca/#demo).</sub>

---

## Why PadSpan?

Most BLE presence integrations give you a config flow and a sensor. PadSpan gives you a **complete tracking workstation** — floor plan editor, room boundary polygons, 3D isometric maps, walk-around calibration, follow mode with alerts to your phone or email, a training hub, and a full sample/demo mode so you can explore every feature before plugging in hardware.

It works with your existing BLE scanners. HA Bluetooth proxies (ESPHome, or Shelly Gen2+ set as a Bluetooth scanner, the same ones Bermuda uses) and Home Assistant's own Bluetooth are picked up directly; ESPresense nodes come in over MQTT, which you switch on in **Manage → HA Entities → ESPresense MQTT** and which needs HA's MQTT integration configured. ESP32s running Tasmota with Bluetooth come in over MQTT the same way (experimental: **Manage → HA Entities → Tasmota BLE**). No custom firmware. No cloud dependency. The tracking runs locally.

---

## Screenshots

### Running on the wall

Not a mockup — this is PadSpan on a wall panel in daily use, next to the
thermostat and light switches.

---

| ![Full-screen 3D map with pan/zoom, floating stats, scanner sonar, and tracked device strip](./images/purelive-immersive.png) | ![NVR-style replay with 3D map, timeline scrubber, and distance travelled per device](./images/traceback-playback-3d.png) |

| Sandbox Developer Tools | Floor Plan Editor |
|:-:|:-:|

---

## Feature Highlights

### Presence Tracking
- Room-level BLE device tracking (5-second refresh)
- **Follow mode** — animated room map + movement timeline for any tracked device
- Multi-device simultaneous tracking with per-device movement alerts to your phone or email (60 s rate limit)
- Kalman-filtered RSSI smoothing (replaces simple moving averages)
- Home/away detection: each named device's `device_tracker` is `home` (its state is the room) or `not_home`
- **Phone & watch tracking** — guided setup wizard with [irk-capture](https://github.com/DerekSeaman/irk-capture) integration, HA Companion App iBeacon for Android, and IRK resolution for Apple devices
- Private BLE address resolution (iBeacon UUID + IRK support)
- **Occupancy estimation** — people in the building, never devices: HA person entities (one per phone), unclaimed phones and watches recognised on the air by their rotating addresses and clustered by RSSI co-location, and occupancy/motion sensors by room; tagged things are listed, not counted

### Device Identity
- **Stable device identity (padspan_id)** — every physical device gets an immutable ID that survives MAC rotation, iBeacon UUID changes, and firmware updates
- O(1) identity resolution from any volatile key (MAC, iBeacon, canonical_id)
- Automatic migration from older object/tag systems
- Interactive device registry: merge duplicates, add identities, relabel, delete

### Floor Plans & Maps
- Upload a floor plan picture (PNG, JPG, GIF, BMP, WebP or SVG; a photo of a sketch works) or a PDF (you pick the page), or start from a phone's room scan or a blank floor
- **Two-point measure tool** for precise real-world scale calibration with aspect ratio validation
- Draw room boundary polygons directly over blueprints
- Multi-floor **3D isometric visualization** with live object positions
- **2D flat map mode** with zoom/pan and toggle filters (scanners, tagged, unknown, rooms)
- Drag-and-place scanner markers with 3-digit radio IDs
- Auto-detect stale or missing radios on your map
- Line up floors in 3D Stack: each plan keeps its own place in metres (there is no master map)

### Calibration
- Walk-around fingerprint collection from the panel's **Calibration** screen, on a phone, tablet or computer
- k-NN fingerprint matching + OLS path-loss model fitting per scanner
- Coverage heatmap with guided "walk here next" target suggestions
- Leave-one-out cross-validation for model quality scoring
- 3D isometric tune view with draggable receiver markers

### Multi-Floor Intelligence
- **Floor-transition learning** — adaptive dwell-based velocity gate prevents phantom floor changes
- Learned cross-floor RSSI attenuation
- Outdoor penalties for rooms on an Outside floor: while a device is indoors, readings for an outdoor room count 15 dB weaker, and a move between indoors and outdoors needs every vote in the window unless the position on the map agrees

### Phone & Watch Tracking

Tracking phones is the hardest problem in BLE presence — they rotate their Bluetooth address every ~15 minutes specifically to prevent tracking. PadSpan offers multiple paths depending on your device:

| Device | Easiest Method | What You Need |
|--------|---------------|---------------|
| **Android phone** | HA Companion App iBeacon | Install app, enable BLE Transmitter. Done. |
| **iPhone / iPad** | IRK via [irk-capture](https://github.com/DerekSeaman/irk-capture) | Spare ESP32, flash irk-capture, pair once, paste IRK |
| **Apple Watch** | IRK via irk-capture | Same as iPhone — pair watch to irk-capture ESP32 |
| **Beacon or key tag with a fixed ID or address** | Automatic | Name it once and the name sticks. [Which Bluetooth tag works?](https://padspan.traks.ca/guides/bluetooth-tags/) has what to buy and how to test a tag. Older Tiles work this way; Life360 is moving newer ones to changing addresses, so test yours |
| **AirTag and other Find My tags** | Probabilistic (experimental) | Enable **MAC Rotation Bridging** in Settings → Features. They change address every 15 min near their owner's iPhone and once a day away from it, with no stable identifier, so bridging links a named tag to its next address when it's clear which one it is. It works while the tag stays in range, won't guess between two tags together, and a tag that was out of range when it changed comes back nameless. **Apple Device Classification** only adds a label |
| **SmartTag** (Samsung) | Not reliably | No stable identifier in the air. MAC Rotation Bridging has only a fingerprint to go on |
| **AirPods** | Apple auto-classification | Detected and labeled automatically when feature enabled (display only — does not solve identity) |

The **Phone Setup Wizard** (experimental) shows the three ways in for a phone. For irk-capture it asks the device's name and whose it is first, then picks up the key the ESP32 shows in Home Assistant; [Which room is my phone in?](https://padspan.traks.ca/guides/phone-room-presence/) walks through it.

For devices where you can't get an IRK, the experimental **MAC Rotation Bridging** feature matches advertisement patterns across address rotations to maintain tracking continuity.

> **Acknowledgement:** The IRK extraction workflow is built on [Derek Seaman's irk-capture](https://github.com/DerekSeaman/irk-capture) — an ingenious ESP32 tool that emulates BLE peripherals to extract Identity Resolving Keys during pairing. It's what makes practical phone tracking in Home Assistant possible without rooting devices or owning a Mac.

### Scanner Hardware & Management
- **Tested with 20+ ESP32 boards** — the antenna matters more than the chip. Boards with full-size external antennas consistently outperform chip/PCB antennas for room-level accuracy
- Top picks: ESP32-S3 with Ethernet + antenna, ESP32-S3 with WiFi + antenna, ESP32-C3 with antenna
- Auto-discover BLE scanners from Home Assistant integrations
- Per-scanner signal quality metrics and coverage analysis
- WiFi SSID, IP address, and connection type display
- Assign scanners to floors and rooms on the map

### Alerts & Automation
- Alerts when a device changes room, arrives or leaves (per device, 60-second rate limit on room changes), sent through Home Assistant's own notify services: the Companion app for a phone, or a mail integration such as SMTP for email. PadSpan has no mailer of its own, so set those up in Home Assistant first
- HA entities: **device trackers** (the state is the room, or `not_home`), **area sensors**, **distance sensors**, and binary sensors for Vacation Mode, guests at home and sub-zones
- Home Assistant events when a named device arrives or leaves (`padspan_device_arrived`, `padspan_device_departed`) and when a followed one changes room (`padspan_room_change`), for your own automations

### Analytics
- **Insights** (a Traceback mode) — per-object time-in-room and entry-count tables, plus peak concurrent occupancy, with CSV/JSON export
- **Busy Times** (a Traceback mode, PadSpan Pro) — which rooms are busiest overall and by hour of day, aggregated across every tracked object over a 1/3/7-day range
- **Locate** (a Follow option, PadSpan Pro) — room-by-room wayfinding to the device or person you're following, from wherever your own tracked phone currently is; a live metre-distance readout once you're in the same room. No compass, no camera — routed over your own room-adjacency map, refreshed on every live poll like Follow

### Atlas — The Device Map
Formerly "Lights" — renamed because it outgrew the name. One isometric map of every floor, drawn the way an electrician draws a lighting plan, for placing and controlling real devices rather than just tracking BLE:
- **Fixtures** — lights, fans, locks, and motion, temperature, humidity, air-quality and flood sensors, each placed at their real position, shape, size and rotation
- **Smoke, gas and CO alarms** on the map beside leak sensors — an alarm rings its room red, shows on every PadSpan screen and stays up for 2 days or until someone resets it
- **WLED control** — brightness, colour and effects live from the map
- **Outdoor gear** — anything HA puts on an Outside floor (shed, garden, driveway) places on the real floor plate just outside the room it lives beside, instead of falling off the map
- **Doors & windows** as real RF barriers — material-aware attenuation (steel blocks harder than hollow-core), live open/closed state, and an **Invert** toggle for a sensor that reports backwards. A cover (garage door, gate, blind), switch, button or script that opens it, and its lock, can be linked to the same door or window, for one card with its state, Open/Close and the lock
- **Automorph** — a soft aura drawn on the map from a fixture into its room, in a growing set of distinct styles (Glow, Blueprint, Nebula, Halo, Bloom and more). It changes how the map looks, not what the lights do
- **Showcase** — 20 curated visual themes for the map itself, with a presets bar to save and load a look
- **Scene row** — under the map, a tile for each Home Assistant scene that sets a placed light, drawn as a small map of the lights it uses; a tap runs it
- **Heatmap** (PadSpan Pro, off by default) — colours each room by its own temperature, humidity or CO₂ sensors
- A **hover HUD** names what's under the cursor (or a touch hold) with every stacked marker as a clickable row; **Alt+click** cycles the stack when several devices sit on top of each other
- Full touch support — pinch-zoom, drag and tap are tuned for a wall panel or phone, not just a mouse

See the [Atlas Guide](./docs/ATLAS_GUIDE.md) for a full walkthrough, and the [Live Aboard Guide](./docs/LIVE_ABOARD_GUIDE.md) for the 3D house (Pro). Placement, Automorph and Showcase are PadSpan Pro (or [PadSpan Bright Pro](https://github.com/gbroeckling/padspanBright)) features — see [Editions](#editions) below; a free install still gets floors, rooms and a tap-to-toggle marker per light.

### UI & Experience
- **Live Tracker mode** — immersive full-screen 3D dashboard with pan/zoom, floating glass overlays, and collapsible info panels
- **23 dedicated views** with Basic and Advanced modes
- **Guided setup** with progress tracking
- Dark forest-green theme designed for always-on displays
- Built-in **Training Hub** with 16 animated walkthroughs + full manual
- **Sample mode** — fully functional demo with synthetic data, no hardware needed
- Calibration is a screen of the main panel that you can open on a phone during walk-around collection
- **NVR-style movement playback** — replay tracked device movement on the 3D map

### Experimental Features (Settings → Features)
- **Phone Setup Wizard** — guided flow for tracking phones and watches. Points to [irk-capture](https://github.com/DerekSeaman/irk-capture) for IRK extraction. Also shows the easy Android path (HA Companion App iBeacon) and Apple IRK options. Credit to [Derek Seaman](https://github.com/DerekSeaman) for the excellent irk-capture tool that makes IRK extraction practical for everyone.
- **MAC Rotation Bridging** — when a phone's Bluetooth address rotates (every ~15 min), PadSpan matches advertisement characteristics (company ID, services, signal pattern) to tentatively link old and new addresses. Bridges the tracking gap without requiring an IRK. Probabilistic — may occasionally link wrong devices.
- **Apple Device Classification** — shows what sent an Apple Find My signal (AirTag, a Find My accessory, which can be another brand's tag or AirPods, or an Apple device such as an iPhone, iPad or Mac) instead of just "Find My", in Devices, Bluetooth → Advertisements and a device's details. It can't tell an iPhone from an iPad or a Watch: nothing Apple sends over Bluetooth says which. Display-only — does not affect tracking or identity.
- **Radio Map** — RSSI heatmap overlay using inverse distance weighting
- **Signal distortion map** — where positions matched to calibration points (k-NN) disagree with reality
- **Walk-to-Identify** — discover unknown devices by correlating walking motion
- **RoomPlan Import** — import an Apple RoomPlan scan (a `.usdz` file, or RoomPlan JSON) in Mapping → Layout, as rooms to review before anything is saved
- **Robot Vacuum Import** — import a robot vacuum's map (Valetudo, Dreame or Xiaomi) in Mapping → Layout as a floor plan with its rooms
- **iPhone Setup Path** — walks an iPhone through getting its IRK, adding it and checking it resolves (on by default for a new install)
- **RSSI Vector Capture** — record what every scanner heard, poll by poll, to replay a walk offline against changed settings

---

## How It Compares

[Bermuda](https://github.com/agittins/bermuda) and [ESPresense](https://espresense.com/) are both good, and lots of people run them. This is what each does, from their own docs as of October 2026 ([more detail](https://padspan.traks.ca/guides/bermuda-vs-espresense/)). If something here is out of date, [open an issue](https://github.com/gbroeckling/padspanHA/issues) and it gets fixed.

| | PadSpan HA | Bermuda | ESPresense (+ Companion) |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Room-level presence | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Hardware | ESPHome Bluetooth proxies, Shelly Gen2+, HA's own Bluetooth or a USB adapter, or ESPresense over MQTT once switched on | ESPHome Bluetooth proxies, Shelly Gen2+, USB adapters | Its own firmware on ESP32 nodes |
| Floor plan needed? | No: rooms come from each scanner's HA area; the map is optional | No | No for rooms; Companion's map needs your rooms as coordinates (YAML, or made with MagicPlan or its Floorplan Creator) |
| Map of your home | ✅ draw rooms on your floor plan | — | ✅ Companion |
| Multi-floor 3D view | ✅ (the full 3D house, Live Aboard, is Pro) | — (has a Floor sensor) | ✅ Companion |
| Position between scanners | ✅ with 3+ scanners placed on a measured plan | — | ✅ Companion (X/Y/Z) |
| Calibration | Walk-around fingerprints and per-scanner signal fit | Guided: global, per proxy and per device | Manual on each node; automatic in Companion |
| Signal smoothing | Kalman filter plus a room vote | Averaging, a speed limit on moving away, and area hysteresis | Filtering on the node, Kalman on position (Companion) |
| iPhones and Apple Watches (IRK) | ✅ via Private BLE Device or irk-capture, with a setup guide | ✅ via Private BLE Device | ✅ enrolled on the node's web page |
| Tags that change address (AirTag, SmartTag) | Experimental | — | — (AirTags can only be counted) |
| HA room, distance and tracker entities | ✅ | ✅ | A room sensor with distance; a tracker from Companion |
| Movement history | ✅ playback (Traceback) | HA's own history, no playback | Path view in Companion (its history logging is in beta) |
| Alerts when a device changes room | ✅ built in (Follow) | With your own HA automations | With your own HA automations |
| Where you set it up | A PadSpan panel in the HA sidebar | Home Assistant's setup dialogs | The node's web page and the Companion app |
| Try it before installing | ✅ [browser demo](https://padspan.traks.ca/demo/) and a sample house | — | — |

Room Assistant isn't in the table: its last release was in March 2022.

Already running Bermuda? Keep it: PadSpan runs next to it on the same proxies and leaves it as it is. [Bermuda and PadSpan together](https://padspan.traks.ca/guides/bermuda/) explains how.

Looking at NeonPlan 3D too? It added room presence to its free 3D floor plan in October. [Bermuda, NeonPlan 3D or PadSpan?](https://padspan.traks.ca/guides/bermuda-vs-neonplan/) compares all three.

---

## Editions

The presence tracking on this page is **PadSpan HA**: free, GPL v3, no key required.
A licence key unlocks the rest on the *same install*: nothing to reinstall,
nothing to reconfigure.

| Edition | Key | What it is |
|---------|:---:|------------|
| **PadSpan HA** | none | Room presence, plans, calibration, movement history and the sensors for your automations. Free forever. |
| **PadSpan Pro** | `pro` | Every gated feature in PadSpan HA — Atlas device placement (shape, size, angle, WLED, Automorph, Showcase), Live Aboard (the 3D house, experimental) with Furnish, wall mode, Whole House Presets and Vacation Mode, Forensics, Busy Times, Locate, and anything gated later. |
| [**PadSpan Bright**](https://github.com/gbroeckling/padspanBright) | none | A separate, lighter HACS listing generated from this same source — just the Atlas device map, for anyone who wants light control without the BLE presence tracking. |
| **PadSpan Bright Pro** | `bright` | Bright's full Atlas toolset (placement, shapes, WLED, Automorph, Showcase), priced separately from PadSpan Pro. |

No key yet? **Settings → Features → PadSpan licence** has a one-time 90-day free trial — no card required, no reinstall; it needs the opt-in usage report on, and the report stays on until the trial ends. A PadSpan Pro key also unlocks Bright's tools if you install Bright instead — one key, either download. Pricing and purchase: [padspan.traks.ca](https://padspan.traks.ca).

---

## Installation

[![Open PadSpan in your Home Assistant](https://my.home-assistant.io/badges/hacs_repository.svg)](https://my.home-assistant.io/redirect/hacs_repository/?owner=gbroeckling&repository=padspanHA&category=integration)

The button opens PadSpan in the Marketplace on Home Assistant 2026.11 and newer, and in HACS on older versions.

### From the Marketplace (Home Assistant 2026.11 and newer)

1. Open **Settings → Marketplace** and search for **PadSpan**
2. Open **PadSpan HA** and choose **Install**. The first time, the Marketplace asks you to confirm that what it lists isn't reviewed by the Home Assistant project
3. The setup dialog opens right away, with no restart. Choose **Submit**
4. Open **PadSpan HA** in the sidebar

### Via HACS (Home Assistant 2026.10 and older)

1. Open HACS in your Home Assistant instance
2. Search for and install **PadSpan HA** (it's in the HACS default list, no custom repository needed)
3. **Restart Home Assistant completely** (Settings → System → Restart)
4. Add the integration: Settings → Devices & Services → Add Integration → PadSpan HA

### Manual

1. Download `padspan_ha.zip` from the [latest release](https://github.com/gbroeckling/padspanHA/releases/latest)
2. In your HA config folder, make the folder `custom_components/padspan_ha` and unzip `padspan_ha.zip` into it. The zip's files have no folder of their own: when you are done, `manifest.json` is at `custom_components/padspan_ha/manifest.json`
3. Restart Home Assistant
4. Add the integration: Settings → Devices & Services → Add Integration → PadSpan HA

## Requirements

- Home Assistant **2024.8** or newer
- A machine with **more than 2 GB of RAM** is recommended (a Raspberry Pi 4 or 5 with 4 GB or more, or similar). Near a busy street PadSpan hears thousands of passing devices, and on a 2 GB Pi Home Assistant can run out of memory within hours. See [Minimum requirements](./docs/MINIMUM_REQUIREMENTS.md)
- At least one BLE scanner: an ESPHome Bluetooth proxy, a Shelly Gen2 or newer set as a Bluetooth scanner, your Home Assistant machine's own Bluetooth, ESPresense nodes (they also need HA's MQTT integration, and the ingestion switched on in Manage → HA Entities), or Tasmota devices (experimental, over MQTT)
- The Marketplace (built into Home Assistant from 2026.11) or HACS, for easy installation and updates

## Quick Start

1. Install from the Marketplace (or with HACS, then restart HA)
2. Add the PadSpan HA integration
3. Open the **PadSpan HA** panel in the sidebar. **Who's where now** puts each device in the room of the scanner that hears it best, from each scanner's Home Assistant area. No floor plan needed. From 0.38.276, a scanner with no area gets a room to choose right on that card, guessed from its name when it can be: pick it and choose **Set room**
4. Name your phones and tags: [Which room is my phone in?](https://padspan.traks.ca/guides/phone-room-presence/) shows how for iPhone, Apple Watch and Android
5. **Preview a finished house** shows a sample house with every feature set up. **Back to my house** returns to yours
6. Want the map? **Make it a map** walks you through it: upload a floor plan, set its scale, draw rooms, place scanners, then **Put it on the map**, track your phone or watch (a step of its own from 0.38.276) and calibrate

Every step, with pictures: [From the Marketplace to your first room](https://padspan.traks.ca/guides/get-started/).

## What PadSpan never touches

PadSpan reads your other integrations and leaves them as they are. Installing, disabling, reloading or removing it doesn't change another integration's devices, entities or config entries (Private BLE Device, Bermuda, ESPresense, the Companion App or any other). A repo test fails if new code tries to. One thing is Home Assistant's own doing: before Home Assistant 2026.8, it filed PadSpan's sensors under another integration's device with the same Bluetooth address. PadSpan 0.38.162 no longer lets that happen, but a device merged that way before stays merged.

- **Reads:** HA areas and floors, the device and entity registries, Bluetooth advertisements, entity states, and Private BLE Device / Companion App entries (only to name a phone's rotating address).
- **Creates:** its own config entry, its own `padspan_ha` entities and devices, and its own `.storage/padspan_ha.*` files.
- **Never changes on its own:** anything belonging to another integration. The only exceptions are buttons you press, one at a time: Add IRK / Delete from HA (Private BLE), Manage → Delete an entity or area, assigning a radio or light to a room, and Enable & Track for a phone's BLE Transmitter.
- **Uninstalling removes:** PadSpan's own entities and devices, and gives WLED lights their sync back. Its `.storage` files stay (Manage → Factory Reset clears your setup from them first). An IRK you added stays in Private BLE Device.

Details: [What PadSpan never touches](./docs/GETTING_STARTED.md#what-padspan-never-touches).

## Security

Names from devices, scanners and rooms are always shown as plain text in the panel. Backups, restores, factory reset, IRKs, map uploads and anything that sends data out of the house need a Home Assistant administrator. For homes where other people have accounts, **Settings → Tracking → Enhanced security** (on for a new install, off in a home set up before November 2026 until someone turns it on; admin-only) makes every change to PadSpan's shared setup need an administrator as well, while the household can still view and use PadSpan. See [Who can change what](./docs/GETTING_STARTED.md#who-can-change-what) and [SECURITY.md](./SECURITY.md) to report an issue.

## Updates & Privacy

Once a day, PadSpan asks `padspan.traks.ca` whether a newer version is available and shows a Home Assistant notification when one is. The request contains **only your installed version number** (e.g. `?v=0.21.10`). Like any web request, the server sees your IP address; nothing else is sent, no identifiers are stored on your system, and no usage data is collected. On its own, this check gives the project only a count of requests, not of installs: installs are counted only by the opt-in usage report's random install ID and, for a licence key, by the licence check (both below).

The answer can also switch PadSpan's free-Pro offers (becoming a tester, and invites) off or back on, so an offer that has ended disappears from the panel without an update. It only ever carries those two on/off switches; it cannot add anything to the panel. While the tester offer is on and no licence key is entered, the update notification has one line about it.

To turn it off: **Settings → Tracking → Update Check → Disabled**. That stops the version check.

If a licence key is entered (a trial or a purchase), PadSpan also checks it once a day with `traks.ca`, whether or not Update Check is on. That request sends the key and Home Assistant's instance ID (the licence server keeps only a one-way hash of the ID), both in the body of the request rather than in its address, so a refunded or revoked key stops working. Since 0.38.160 it also sends what tells one licence's homes apart: this home's current token (a random code the licence server gave it), the PadSpan version, the name you gave this home (if any), and whether this home's usage report is on. With no key entered, there is no licence check. The usage report below is sent only if you opt in.

**Device makers.** PadSpan names a device's maker from what the device itself broadcasts and from lists built into PadSpan (Bluetooth's official company and service numbers, and IEEE's list of address makers). Nothing is sent anywhere for this. The address list counts as fact only for an address a Bluetooth receiver has confirmed is fixed and maker-assigned (ESPHome proxies on version 2022.12 or newer and Home Assistant's own Bluetooth say so, and PadSpan remembers it across restarts, until a Factory Reset). Shelly, ESPresense and Tasmota don't say, so there a match reads "Probably". An address a receiver reports as random is never looked up.

**The shared furniture library.** Live Aboard (Pro) can swap furniture with other PadSpan homes through a library at `padspan.traks.ca/api/furniture_library.php`. It is off by default and only an administrator can turn it on (**Settings → Atlas → Live Aboard → Shared library**); while it is off, nothing goes there. While it is on, Home Assistant sends a request only when someone uses the library:

- **A search**: the words typed, the filters and sort order picked, and which page of results.
- **A look at one piece**: that piece's library ID, and whether it was placed (the library counts placings; the request says nothing about who placed it).
- **A report**: the piece's library ID, one of two reasons, and six random characters that stand for this home in the library.
- **A share** (after the library's terms are accepted): the piece's recipe, which is its kind, builder settings, colours, width, depth and height, and its details sheet (category, room, style, material and the like, with a title, brand and model if it has them). With it go a random submission ID that carries this home's six characters, a random owner token made for that share, the terms version and the PadSpan version. Where the piece stands, its name in your house and the device it is are not part of a share. Text that looks like an email address, a web or street address, a phone number or a key is refused before anything is sent. A share made while the library can't be reached waits in Home Assistant and goes after the next search or look the library answers.
- **Withdraw** (an administrator): the submission IDs and owner tokens of what this home shared, which is how the library knows to take them out.

Never a photo, a floor plan or the usage report's install ID. As with any web request, the server sees your IP address.

**AI reads.** PadSpan has no AI of its own and sends nothing to an AI service itself. A few features can ask an AI you have set up in Home Assistant: an AI Task, which an administrator picks in **Settings → AI**. None is picked by default, and with none picked nothing is read. Every read is a call to Home Assistant's own `ai_task.generate_data` on that AI Task, carrying one picture, instructions that are written into PadSpan (they add only the picture's size in pixels and, for a photo, the kind of piece you picked) and, for a photo, the list of fields to fill in. PadSpan adds no names, addresses or positions from your house; the picture goes as it is, so whatever is printed on a floor plan goes with it. Home Assistant hands the read to the AI behind the AI Task: one that runs in your home, such as Ollama, keeps the picture there, and a cloud one sends it to that company. For the length of the call the picture is a file in a hidden folder in Home Assistant's media folder, removed when the call ends.

A read happens only when someone starts it, never on a schedule:

- **Furniture, a tag, a receiver or a person's figure from a photo** (Live Aboard, Pro; on unless switched off in Settings → AI): the photo you chose. PadSpan keeps no copy of it.
- **Stairs from your floor plans** (Live Aboard, Pro; off by default): one placed floor plan, resized.
- **Add data via plans** and **Build from plans** (Live Aboard, Pro; experimental, off by default, started by an administrator): your placed floor plans, each whole and as crops or tiles of it. Build from plans needs Claude Opus 5.5 or newer through Home Assistant's Anthropic integration.
- **Let Claude draw your rooms** (Pro, started by an administrator, the same Claude): the floor plans of the floor you chose, read the same way. It has no switch in Settings: nothing is read until it is started from its own screen. Once started, it first sends one connection check: a blank one-pixel picture with the words "This is a connection check. Reply with the single word OK."

One photo or plan can take several reads. If a backup AI Task is picked, PadSpan first opens and closes one connection to the main AI Task's server (where its integration keeps an address, as Ollama's does) to see whether it is there; nothing is sent on it.

### Help improve PadSpan (opt-in usage report)

PadSpan is developed against one house. Features that only exist in yours — an iPhone with an IRK, a Bermuda install, twelve floors, a lighting-only setup — never get seen unless someone shares that they exist. So there is an **opt-in, off-by-default** usage report: **Settings → Tracking → Help improve PadSpan**. The panel asks for it **once** — in the setup checklist on a new install, or as a card on Overview for an install that finished setup before the switch existed — with the Preview right there; either answer ends the asking, and the switch stays in Settings either way. One optional question, where you heard about PadSpan, is asked once per install, with a Skip button: on that card after a yes, or on the Overview after the report is turned on in Settings or a free trial, a tester sign-up or a free year starts. An answer or Skip ends it for good. A house whose report was already on is not asked; the same choice is in Settings.

When you opt in, at most once a day PadSpan POSTs a small JSON report (usually about 7 KB, hard cap 32 KB) to `padspan.traks.ca` containing **counts, versions and flags only** — the complete list:

- `schema`, `version`, `edition`, `tier`, `ha_version`, `python`, the UTC `day`, and the random `install_id`
- `licence_group`: only with a licence key used on more than two homes, 16 hex characters made from the key (never the key itself), the same in each home of that licence, so one licence's homes are seen together. A licence's first two homes always count; with more than two homes, every home must keep its report on, and if one turns it off, the key drops back to its first two homes after 14 days
- `country` and `language`: the two-letter country code and the language tag (such as `en-GB`) set in Home Assistant under Settings → System → General, left out when blank. Never looked up from your IP address
- `env`: how many scanners (and how many with diagnostics / ESPresense / other; how many lost, disabled or excluded), floors, rooms, placed lights (and placed devices by kind: lights, fans, locks, motion, door, leak, smoke/gas/CO alarm, temperature, humidity and air-quality sensors, other), walls, maps, positioned scanners and beacons, calibration points (and how many were automatic, and how many have no floor), how many floors carry a real storey height, how many rooms are given their own height (taller than their floor) and, only from a house with a split level, how many rooms are raised above or sunk below the rest of their floor (counts, never which rooms or by how much), and how many scanners carry a mounting height, IRKs, followed devices, Apple Find My addresses on the air right now by type (AirTag / Find My accessory / AirPods / Apple device) and how many of those are away from their owner, with MAC Rotation Bridging on, the Find My tags PadSpan follows by type (how many are on the air, how many have been carried to a new address), objects (total, identified, and by kind), and how many config entries of each related integration (private_ble_device, bermuda, esphome, mqtt, bluetooth, mobile_app, ibeacon, espresense); the two settings that size the object list (how many days an unidentified object stays in the history, and the oldest advert the live snapshot takes); and `hw`, the class of machine: how many CPUs, total RAM as a bucket (up to 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 / 16 GB, or more), the CPU architecture (x86_64 / aarch64 / armv7 ...), the installation type (OS / Supervised / Container / Core) and the board family (Raspberry Pi 2–5, Home Assistant Green or Yellow, ODROID, Tinker, Khadas, a VM, generic x86-64 or aarch64) — each from a fixed list, anything else reported as `other` or `unknown`; never a model string, hostname or serial; and `temp_fresh`, for the temperature and humidity sensors placed on the map: how many there are, how many reported within the hour by each of Home Assistant's three clocks (last changed, last updated, last reported), how many carry a last-reported time at all, and how long ago they last reported, in fixed buckets (under 5 minutes, 5–15, 15–60 minutes, 1–6 hours, over 6) — counts only, never a sensor, a room or a reading; and, only from a house with quiet mode on, `quiet_hidden`: roughly what share of the objects quiet mode hides (under 25%, 25–50%, 50–75%, over 75%); and, only from a house with two screens or more, a short list of words for each of its first five screens (what its Overview drew, kiosk / full screen / windowed, its resolution class and kind of device), never an id; and, only if you chose to answer, `heard_from`: where you heard about PadSpan, one word from a fixed list (Reddit, YouTube, the Home Assistant forum, another forum, the Marketplace or HACS, GitHub, Discord, a web search, a friend, somewhere else). It is your own answer, never worked out from anything, and Settings → Tracking changes or clears it; `store`: which store keeps this copy of PadSpan up to date, as one word (Home Assistant's Marketplace, HACS, neither because it was copied in by hand, or unknown when the store could not be read); and `used_in`: how many automations and how many scripts use one of PadSpan's entities or devices, two counts, never which ones; and `power_teams`, only from a house with a power team or a colour bulb: how many power teams (smart bulbs fed by a wall dimmer or switch, run as one light), how many have a wall control and whether it is a light or a switch and which integration runs it, how many turn off by cutting the power and how many by turning the bulbs off, how many follow the day, have their own curve or moved sun times, how many wake someone and how long the wake-up fades (in bands), how many bulbs are in teams (and per team, in bands) and their brands and integrations; and, team or not, how many colour bulbs of each brand (Hue, IKEA, Innr, LIDL, Ledvance, WiZ, Tuya and others, from a fixed list; anything else is `other`) and each integration the house has. Counts and fixed words only, never a team's name, an entity id, a wake-up time or a maker's own words

**If you delete PadSpan** from Home Assistant while the report is on, it sends one last report that says so: the anonymous ID, the day, the PadSpan version and the flag `integration_removed`, with nothing about the house. It is how a removed install is told from a machine that is switched off. With the report off, nothing is sent.

**Never**: MAC addresses (in any notation), IRKs or licence keys, device / room / floor / entity names or ids, IP addresses, coordinates, or timestamps finer than the day. The report carries a random install ID so installs can be counted rather than pings — replace it any time with **New anonymous ID**. **Preview what would be sent** shows the report exactly as it stands (same fields and values a send made that second would carry), before or after opting in. Before every send the code walks every value and refuses the whole report if it finds a MAC / UUID / 32-hex / licence-key / IP / email / entity-id shape or any string over 64 characters, or any key or word in `hw` / `perf` / `runs` / `quiet_errors` that is not on their fixed lists; `tests/test_telemetry.py` builds a report from a house full of names, MACs, UUIDs, keys and coordinates and proves none of them are in it. Opting in is an administrator action; the usage and error windows start at the moment you opt in, so nothing from before it goes.

**Invites.** Now and then the developer invites some installs that send the report to try something, such as a free year of PadSpan Pro. The developer picks them by their anonymous install ID, and the invite comes back in the reply to that install's next report: a random one-use token and a last day, kept in Home Assistant where an administrator's panel sees only that an invite is open (never the token). It shows as a card on Overview and in **Settings → Features → PadSpan licence**. Nothing is sent unless you press a button: **Claim** sends the token and the email you type to the licence server at traks.ca, which emails you the key; your email goes to the developer, as a purchase's does, and is never shared. **No thanks** sends the token alone, so the invite is never sent again. The invite list keeps only whether an invite was claimed or declined, never the email.

#### Become a tester (separate from the usage report)

While the report is on, the same card offers **Become a tester**, for anyone happy to be contacted about trying new things before they ship. Testers get PadSpan Pro free for two years, sent by email to the address they sign up with, for as long as the usage report stays on. It is the one place PadSpan asks for contact details, so it is kept apart from the anonymous report in every way: its own consent box, its own **Send sign-up** button, its own address (`padspan.traks.ca/api/tester.php`) and its own random tester ID — never the report's install ID. What goes is what you enter — an email address (required), a GitHub username and a name (optional), what you would like to test, notes and a time zone — plus the **About your setup** lines you leave ticked: counts and versions only, the same kind as the report, each one untickable. **Preview what will be sent** shows the exact JSON first, and notes that look like a key or token are refused. Your anonymous reports are tied to the sign-up only if you tick **Link my anonymous usage reports** (untick it and send an update to undo). Nothing is sent except when you press a button, and nothing is retried. It goes to the developer only, is kept until you withdraw, and is never shared or sold; the server sees your IP address as it does for any web request, but it is not stored with your sign-up. **Stop being a tester** deletes your sign-up from the server, and it is removed from your Home Assistant once the server confirms. That button stays there even if you later turn the report off, and a factory reset or restore keeps your sign-up, so you can always withdraw it. Signing up is an administrator action.
